title: Universal Concept for HDB Flats Built before 2006
what_it_is: Universal Concept for HDB Flats Built before 2006

sections.label: Accessibility features in HDB blocks
sections.summary: Older blocks get accessibility features, lift upgrading, neighbourhood renewal features, and HIP and EASE options like grab bars and ramps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of National Development)
sentences.text: For older blocks, UD and barrier-free design features based on the prevailing Code of Accessibility in the Built Environment are incorporated, where feasible, when the blocks undergo upgrading.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of National Development)
sentences.text: We have also introduced the Lift Upgrading Programme (LUP) to provide direct lift access to HDB residents by adding new lifts and lift shafts to eligible blocks, where feasible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of National Development)
sentences.text: At the precinct level, the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) provides and upgrades features catered to seniors and those with mobility challenges, including ramps, resting points, elderly fitness corners in three-generation playgrounds, as well as wheelchair and elderly-friendly planters in community gardens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of National Development)
sentences.text: To enhance the safety and mobility of seniors in their homes, residents can also choose to install grab bars in their bathrooms or toilets, as well as ramps within their flats and at the main entrance, under the Home Improvement Programme (HIP) and Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programme.

sections.label: Review of EASE programme
sections.summary: The EASE programme is being reviewed to explore additional items for seniors' safety and mobility, considering ageing demographics and future needs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, we are currently reviewing the EASE programme to explore the provision of additional items to further enhance the safety and mobility of our seniors within their flats, taking into consideration the changing demographic profile of the ageing population, as well as anticipating future needs.
